context: Inventory the CLI platform-option vocabulary, adapter consumers, sensitive keys, serialization, and the remote auth/tenancy/admission policy. Design a bounded schema with allow-listed option names and types, per-platform authorization, redaction, size limits, idempotency implications, and durable-job persistence. Decide whether options belong on synchronous local run_benchmark, remote start_benchmark, or both. Implement forwarding only through the validated path, add schema and transport parity tests, update the MCP reference and generated prompt guidance, and reject unknown or secret-bearing options with structured errors.
description: Successor of add-first-class-mcp-platform-option-arguments, promoted from deferral #461 of prompts-landing-phase5-mcp-parity. The MCP benchmark tools currently expose platform, benchmark, scale, mode, phases, and related controls but not the adapter-specific platform options available to the CLI. Define and implement a typed, explicitly authorized MCP contract if remote callers need those options; do not pass an arbitrary dictionary through to platform adapters.

preserves.behavior: CLI platform-option behavior remains unchanged outside the explicit MCP contract
Durable jobs persist only validated bounded option data and never raw credentials or secrets
Existing MCP benchmark calls without platform options remain wire-compatible
Unknown, unbounded, credential-bearing, or tenant-disallowed options are rejected before adapter dispatch

verifications.description: A typed MCP platform-option contract is specified
verifications.expected: exits 1 on an unfixed tree; exits 0 once the bounded contract is specified

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/mcp/test_schemas.py tests/unit/mcp/test_benchmark_tools.py -q
verifications.description: Schema and benchmark tests cover option validation and forwarding
verifications.expected: exits 1 on an unfixed tree if the MCP option contract is absent or unsafe; exits 0 once focused tests pass

verifications.description: Remote integration tests prove policy and durable-job behavior
verifications.expected: exits 1 on an unfixed tree if options bypass auth, tenancy, or durable persistence; exits 0 once the integration suite passes

work_units.evidence: Audited benchbox/core/hooks/platform_hooks.py and CLI option registrations, MCP adapter/job call paths, security middleware allowlists, and MCP tests; bounded non-secret allow-list implemented in benchbox/mcp/schemas.py
work_units.summary: Revalidate CLI platform-option sources, adapter consumers, sensitive fields, and the remote policy boundary

work_units.summary: Specify the typed allow-list, per-platform validation, redaction, limits, persistence, and compatibility contract for local and durable remote benchmark calls
